$comment: SUCCESS:ARC-0090 — MCP adapter: declaration, transport, lifecycle, per-session stdio cap, namespacing, enable/disable scope. scope_decision_table is computed by resolve_enabled, not authored.
title: MCP adapter: transport, lifecycle ownership and per-session multiplication limits
question: Specify the MCP adapter contract: server declaration, transport choice between per-session stdio and a shared HTTP endpoint, lifecycle ownership (who starts, who reaps), the hard limit on processes per session, tool-name namespacing to prevent collisions, and the enable/disable SCOPE semantics - given the measured trap that a disable written at the wrong scope is inert while appearing correct, and that the curated enable state must never be destroyed.

server_id.description: Adapter-facing server id. Must not contain __.

server_declaration.rule: Mount requires a declaration. stdio names command[]; http names url.
server_declaration.missing_declaration: ContractError; the server must not spawn.

stdio.multiplication: N sessions × M stdio servers = N×M processes
stdio.historic_driver: eager per-session stdio MCP multiplication; catalog MEMORY 23 sessions × 65 servers. IMP-0065 reproduced N sessions → N stdio children vs 1 shared HTTP child on this worktree.

http.process_model: one shared child per server_id across sessions
http.multiplication: N sessions × 1 shared HTTP server = 1 process
http.preferred_when: the same server is used by more than one session

transport.choice_rule: The declaration selects transport. The adapter records stdio vs http on every mount. Unrecorded transport is a contract failure.

lifecycle.starts: Adapter.mount is the only start path
lifecycle.session_code_must_not: spawn or kill MCP children directly
lifecycle.shared_http_dead: A dead shared child is a loud error. The session must not hang on stdin or look like a healthy empty tool list (IMP-0065).
lifecycle.memory_guard: A kill-based memory guard must not select a shared-service PID (IMP-0066 / TST-0242).

process_cap.on_exceed: ContractError; refuse to start the extra stdio child
process_cap.rationale: Hard cap stops per-session multiplication from reproducing the commit-exhaustion class even when a caller ignores shared HTTP.

namespacing.why: Bare echo collides when two servers advertise it.

scope_semantics.rule: Walk local, then project, then user. The first scope that names the server_id wins. Unnamed servers default to enabled.
scope_semantics.trap: A disable written at user (root-scoped disabledMcpServers analog) is inert when project or local already names the server. The config file still shows the disable, so the write looks correct.
scope_semantics.inert_disable_example: project enabled=true and user enabled=false — process table still shows the server
two_signals: the configuration file that holds the setting
the live process table showing whether the server actually spawned
scope_semantics.must_not: treat any-scope disable as effective (mutant any_scope_disable)

enable_preservation.rule: Any migration must capture and restore the curated enable/disable map byte-identically (canonical JSON, sorted keys).
enable_preservation.must_not: wipe, reshape, or drop user-authored enable entries
enable_preservation.estate_precedent: TST-0071: root-scoped disabledMcpServers dumps were inert; live curation lived per-project. A schema rename must relocate those values, never destroy them.

consumer_call_site.notes: Probes call Adapter.mount against this draft. TST-0044 is the catalog conformance suite written before broad implementation; its missing ARC-0090.json note is residual, not BLOCKED.

missing_inputs.note: ARC-0077 (owner ratification) is not on this worktree. This contract is specified from the catalog question, TST-0044 executable adapter rules, IMP-0065 process-multiplication measurement, and TST-0071 inert-scope curation. It is not a claim that the owner has ratified a winning architecture.

negative_controls.must: process table still lists the server; config file shows the user disable
process table does not list the server; project file shows disable
mutant refuses to spawn — proving first-scope-wins is what kept the process alive
canonical enable bytes differ after migrate

tests.name: Disable at ineffective scope: config shows it, process table still has the server; effective-scope disable: process gone
Curated enable map captured and restored byte-identically

reviewer.notes: Probes are the consumer-side call site against this draft. An independent human contract reviewer is residual (catalog owner_approval_required=false).

does_not_claim: a production MCP client already wires every path through Adapter
live mcp.json servers were mounted on this box
secret values were read or printed

scope_decision_table.notes: User/root disable is inert while project has an entry. This is the measured trap: a disable that looks correct at the wrong scope.
Project disable is the effective scope; process must not spawn.
With no local/project entry, user disable is effective.
Local disable wins over project enable.
